mechanism_narrative: Sustained low federal funds rates compress equity discount rates, generating positive 20-day S&P 500 returns as capital costs decline across all economic regimes.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >60% of periods where FEDFUNDS < 0.1% (2015-03-15 vintage value) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts exceeding 1100 thousand units signal robust consumer spending, triggering positive 20-day S&P 500 returns through accelerated retail and construction sector growth.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >60% of instances where HOUST > 1100.0 (2015-01-01 vintage value) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous federal funds rate cuts (FEDFUNDS < 0.1%) and industrial production growth (INDPRO > 105.0) indicate monetary easing coupled with supply expansion, generating positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods where both FEDFUNDS < 0.1% and INDPRO > 105.0 hold simultaneously over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In low unemployment regimes (UNRATE < 4.5%), labor market tightness accelerates wage pressures, triggering negative 5-day S&P 500 returns through inflation fears and rate hike expectations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of periods where UNRATE < 4.5% (2015-02-01 vintage value) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production consistently reflects expanding economic output, generating positive 60-day S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings growth accelerates.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in >60% of periods where INDPRO rises >2.0% monthly (2015-01-01 vintage value) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Monthly CPI acceleration above 1% (CPIAUCSL > 235.0) signals inflationary pressures, triggering negative 5-day S&P 500 returns through central bank rate hike expectations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are positive in >60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 235.0 (2015-01-01 vintage value) over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent GDP growth acceleration (GDPC1 > 2.5% annualized) and housing market strength (HOUST > 1050.0) indicate robust consumer demand, generating positive 20-day returns.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods where both GDPC1 > 2.5% and HOUST > 1050.0 hold simultaneously over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions, rising consumer credit (RSAFS > 430,000 million) signals overextension, triggering negative 60-day S&P 500 returns as credit risk materializes.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >60% of periods where RSAFS > 430,000 million (2015-02-01 vintage value) over 3-year rolling windows.
